=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Seller Draft Review Against Buyer Playbook

**Scope:** Review of the Seller's SPA positions (Seller Update) and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003) against the Wattlebridge playbook. This is a negotiation analysis, not a final legal opinion. The Seller's market-context claims are assertions I have not verified.

## Preliminary point: the "FINAL" label

The Seller says these positions were "settled at principal level" and are "not intended to be re-opened." That label does not bind us. Our playbook governs. I have no record of any principal-level agreement to the Seller's figures, and the playbook says the 20%/AUD 4.8m cap and 18-month period may be used only with Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the draft. None has been given. We should not treat the Seller's characterisation as a concession, and we should ask Seller counsel to identify the agreement they are relying on.

## Material departures and pushback

### 1. General warranty cap (Cl 12.1)
- **Seller:** 20% / AUD 4.8m. **Playbook:** 25% / AUD 6m starting position; 20% only as a conditional fallback with Amelia Frost's written authority.
- **Reasoning:** The Seller has anchored at our conditional fallback. Accepting it would concede value we have not authorised.
- **Pushback:** Restate our 25% / AUD 6m position. Do not accept 20% in correspondence. Confirm no fallback will be discussed without Amelia Frost's written approval identifying the draft.

### 2. Thresholds (Cl 12.2)
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000 with recovery only of the excess (deductible).
- **Playbook:** De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded (tipping basket).
- **Reasoning:** The Seller's figures are five times our de minimis and five times our basket, and a deductible structure means the buyer absorbs the first AUD 250,000 of general claims. Combined with the cap, this materially reduces recovery.
- **Pushback:** Reject the deductible structure. Restate AUD 5,000 de minimis and AUD 50,000 tipping basket.

### 3. Claims period (Cl 12.3 / 13)
- **Seller:** 18 months; limitation applies to all Claims "unless expressly stated otherwise."
- **Playbook:** 24 months for general claims; 18 months only with Amelia Frost's written approval. Fundamental/Title claims at least six years.
- **Reasoning:** The 18-month period is an unapproved fallback. The "applies to all Claims" wording is a hidden override that could reduce the Title and Fundamental periods, which the playbook says must stay separate.
- **Pushback:** Restore 24 months for general claims. Delete the blanket "all Claims" wording and confirm that the Fundamental/Title regime sits outside the general time limits.

### 4. Fundamental / Title (Cl 12, "administrative simplicity")
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties.
- **Playbook:** Separate regime; 100% cap; at least six years; outside the general basket, de minimis and buyer-knowledge bar.
- **Reasoning:** This is a central departure. Title to 100% of the shares is the core asset-level protection in a share acquisition. Subjecting it to a 20% cap and 18-month period would leave the buyer exposed to a title defect for a fraction of its value.
- **Pushback:** Reject outright. Reinstate a separate Fundamental/Title regime with a 100% cap, six-year period and no basket, de minimis or knowledge qualifier.

### 5. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance (Cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)
- **Seller:** Apply to "all Claims of any nature."
- **Playbook:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- **Reasoning:** As drafted, the Seller's wording would capture fraud. This is a non-negotiable carve-out.
- **Pushback:** Insert the fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct carve-out expressly. Confirm it applies to all limitation, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions.

### 6. Disclosure (Sch 7; Disclosure Letter 1.1 and 1.2)
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room (to 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and public records.
- **Playbook:** Specific fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Reasoning:** Whole-data-room disclosure would make almost every issue in this package disclosed against us, neutralising warranty protection. It would also effectively defeat the specific indemnities we want (Ironquay, DD-005, DD-006).
- **Pushback:** Reject 1.1 and 1.2 as drafted. Require specific disclosure against identified warranties, with the Seller bearing the burden of making the disclosure fairly and specifically. Disclosure must not qualify Title, Fundamental, fraud or specific indemnity matters.

### 7. Buyer knowledge (Cl 8.3)
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter the Buyer or its advisers "had knowledge" of, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records.
- **Playbook:** Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions. Any qualifier needs named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry, and never excuses title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Reasoning:** This is a second route to excluding claims, and "discoverable" is effectively constructive knowledge of the entire data room. It would also conflict with the specific indemnities we are seeking.
- **Pushback:** Delete 8.3. If any qualifier survives, limit it to named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry, with express carve-outs for title, capacity, fraud and specific indemnities.

### 8. Bluefen change-control consent (Cl 3 / 6.3; DL §2)
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours; consent "satisfied on delivery" of counterparty's written consent. DL confirms no final written consent or evidence that conditions are satisfied.
- **Playbook:** Effective consent and evidence that conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient.
- **Reasoning:** Bluefen is about 30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6m). A consent that is not in hand, with unsatisfied conditions, is a material risk. Deeming it satisfied on delivery shifts that risk to us at Completion.
- **Pushback:** Make effective Bluefen consent plus evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied a condition precedent to Completion. Reject the consent-on-delivery and reasonable-endeavours formulation.

### 9. Riverlark facility (Cl 2 / 7; DL §3)
- **Seller:** Approx. AUD 3.2m outstanding, to be addressed by a release "following Completion." DL confirms the facility is unpaid and no discharge is included.
- **Playbook:** Current payout figure; direct repayment from Completion funds; effective security releases. Any post-completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost approval.
- **Reasoning:** A post-Completion release leaves the Company's assets encumbered with no payment mechanism. This is a Debt-like item that should be repaid at Completion.
- **Pushback:** Require a current payout letter, repayment directly from Completion funds, and executed security releases at Completion. Any post-completion release is off-playbook unless it is secured by an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost approves.

### 10. Employee bonuses (DD-005; funds flow; DL §5)
- **Seller:** AUD 420,000 bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not in the funds flow. DL says on-costs are not addressed.
- **Playbook:** AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Reasoning:** Excluding these from the funds flow means the Company may bear them post-Completion. The Seller's "matter for the Seller" language is not a mechanism.
- **Pushback:** Require the AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs to be a specific funds-flow line item deducted from price, or seller-funded by indemnity. Ask Seller to quantify on-costs (payroll tax, superannuation).

### 11. Ironquay IP (Cl 11.1; DL §4)
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment and "considered adequate." DL notes AUD 180,000 open; no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room.
- **Playbook:** Broaden the narrow indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure. AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way.
- **Reasoning:** The indemnity as drafted covers only the SOW3 payment, leaving IP transfer risk under other SOWs or associated IP claims uncovered. The conditional transfer under DD-004 cl 7.3 means the Project Materials may not be ours until fees are paid.
- **Pushback:** Broaden the indemnity to cover all IP-transfer and ownership risk arising under the Ironquay arrangements, while preserving the SOW3 cure. Require evidence of payment status (receipt or confirmatory assignment). Do not treat AUD 180,000 as confirmed either way.

### 12. Export/privacy incident (DD-006; Cl 4.6 / Sch 6; DL §6)
- **Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter," "not expected to be material."
- **Playbook:** Preserve logs, investigate, require updates. Assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- **Reasoning:** The Seller's materiality characterisation is a conclusion the record does not yet support, since the investigation is ongoing and the scope (~1,240 records, personal information) is unknown. We should not assert a breach either. The playbook position is neutral on outcome and focused on process.
- **Pushback:** Reject "not expected to be material" as a characterisation. Require preservation of logs, completion of the investigation, scope confirmation, regular written updates, and a specific indemnity or escrow mechanism pending the outcome. Do not allege breach or quantify loss.

### 13. Sandbar renewals (DD-008/DD-011; DL §8)
- **Seller:** AUD 330,000 aggregate; "ordinary-course operating costs."
- **Playbook:** Assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Reasoning:** The DL says we cannot tell from the disclosure whether the renewals are unavoidable, terminable or accrued. The Seller's "ordinary course" label is not sufficient to rule them in or out of Debt.
- **Pushback:** Request the renewal terms, termination rights and whether any amounts have accrued. Assess classification on that basis. Do not accept the Seller's characterisation, and do not propose an automatic price deduction.

### 14. Tax and IP (Seller: "settled under the general regime")
- **Playbook:** Tax/IP terms remain OPEN; no unlimited liability assumed; no resolution assumed.
- **Reasoning:** The Seller's statement folds tax and IP into the general regime, which conflicts with keeping categories separate and with leaving those terms open.
- **Pushback:** Reject that tax and IP are settled. Keep them as separate, open categories and note they are subject to our further mark-up.

### 15. Title evidence (DD-012; DL §10)
- **Seller:** Title evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.
- **Playbook:** Require independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence. DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
- **Reasoning:** The register is a Seller-supplied document. The DL itself states the Buyer has not verified title.
- **Pushback:** Require independent evidence: ASIC company extract, certified share transfer history, encumbrance searches (PPSR), and capacity/authority confirmations. Do not accept DD-012 as sufficient on its own.

### 16. Lease and Mossvale (DL §7, §9)
- **Seller:** Lease notification obligation (no landlord consent stated as required); Mossvale assignment restriction (no consent stated as required for sale of shares).
- **Playbook:** Not specifically addressed; assess.
- **Reasoning:** These are not addressed in the playbook positions, but the DL leaves open whether consent is required. Silence is not confirmation.
- **Pushback:** Ask Seller to confirm in writing whether landlord and Mossvale consents are required for the share sale, and to provide the relevant clauses. If consent is required, add it to the conditions.

## Summary of recommendations

1. **Reject the Seller's "FINAL" framing.** Our playbook governs. Ask Seller counsel to identify the principal-level agreement they rely on. Do not concede any fallback without Amelia Frost's written authority.
2. **Restore general cap to 25% / AUD 6m** and reject the 20% anchor.
3. **Restore thresholds:** AUD 5,000 de minimis; AUD 50,000 tipping basket. Reject deductible structure.
4. **Restore 24-month general claims period.** Delete the "all Claims" override.
5. **Reinstate a separate Fundamental/Title regime:** 100% cap, six years, outside the general basket and knowledge bar.
6. **Insert the fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct carve-out** from caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance.
7. **Reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search disclosure.** Require specific fair disclosure.
8. **Delete the blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion (Cl 8.3).**
9. **Bluefen:** Condition Completion on effective consent and evidence the conditions are satisfied. Reject consent-on-delivery.
10. **Riverlark:** Repay at Completion from the funds flow with executed releases. Any post-completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost approval.
11. **Employee bonuses:** AUD 420,000 plus on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item or seller-funded.
12. **Ironquay:** Broaden the indemnity, preserve the SOW3 cure, and require payment-status evidence.
13. **DD-006:** Reject the "not material" characterisation. Require log preservation, investigation, scope confirmation and regular updates. Do not assert breach or quantify loss.
14. **Sandbar renewals:** Obtain terms and assess. No automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
15. **Tax and IP:** Reject "settled" status. Keep open and separate.
16. **Title:** Require independent evidence beyond DD-012.
17. **Lease and Mossvale:** Obtain written confirmation on whether consent is required.

**Immediate next steps:** Send a mark-up responding to each point above; request the principal-level agreement the Seller relies on; and escalate the cap, Title regime and Bluefen/Riverlark points to Amelia Frost, since several involve her written authority.

- **Pushback:** Broaden the indemnity to cover all IP-transfer and ownership risk arising under the Ironquay arrangements, while preserving the SOW3 cure. Require evidence of payment status (receipt or confirmatory assignment). Do not treat AUD 180,000 as confirmed either way.

### 12. Export/privacy incident (DD-006; Cl 4.6 / Sch 6; DL §6)
- **Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter," "not expected to be material."
- **Playbook:** Preserve logs, investigate, require updates. Assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- **Reasoning:** The Seller's materiality characterisation is a conclusion the record does not yet support, since the investigation is ongoing and the scope (~1,240 records, personal information) is unknown. We should not assert a breach either. The playbook position is neutral on outcome and focused on process.
- **Pushback:** Reject "not expected to be material" as a characterisation. Require preservation of logs, completion of the investigation, scope confirmation, regular written updates, and a specific indemnity or escrow mechanism pending the outcome. Do not allege breach or quantify loss.

### 13. Sandbar renewals (DD-008/DD-011; DL §8)
- **Seller:** AUD 330,000 aggregate; "ordinary-course operating costs."
- **Playbook:** Assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Reasoning:** The DL says we cannot tell from the disclosure whether the renewals are unavoidable, terminable or accrued. The Seller's "ordinary course" label is not sufficient to rule them in or out of Debt.
- **Pushback:** Request the renewal terms, termination rights and whether any amounts have accrued. Assess classification on that basis. Do not accept the Seller's characterisation, and do not propose an automatic price deduction.

### 14. Tax and IP (Seller: "settled under the general regime")
- **Playbook:** Tax/IP terms remain OPEN; no unlimited liability assumed; no resolution assumed.
- **Reasoning:** The Seller's statement folds tax and IP into the general regime, which conflicts with keeping categories separate and with leaving those terms open.

### 15. Title evidence (DD-012; DL §10)
- **Seller:** Title evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.
- **Playbook:** Require independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence. DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
- **Reasoning:** The register is a Seller-supplied document. The DL itself states the Buyer has not verified title.
- **Pushback:** Require independent evidence: ASIC company extract, certified share transfer history, encumbrance searches (PPSR), and capacity/authority confirmations. Do not accept DD-012 as sufficient on its own.

### 16. Lease and Mossvale (DL §7, §9)
- **Seller:** Lease notification obligation (no landlord consent stated as required); Mossvale assignment restriction (no consent stated as required for sale of shares).
- **Playbook:** Not specifically addressed; assess.
- **Reasoning:** These are not addressed in the playbook positions, but the DL leaves open whether consent is required. Silence is not confirmation.
- **Pushback:** Ask Seller to confirm in writing whether landlord and Mossvale consents are required for the share sale, and to provide the relevant clauses. If consent is required, add it to the conditions.
